title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Site Ops, and Top Issues
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview:

This document is the canonical playbook for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation supporting Redwood Inference SDKs, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical fixes for our top support issues. It consolidates ownership, templates, publishing workflows, and the most common troubleshooting steps that reduce time-to-resolution for customers and internal teams.

Goals:
- Ensure SDK guides and quickstarts are consistent, discoverable, and runnable by engineers within 10 minutes.
- Keep API examples accurate and idiomatic for Python, JavaScript/Node, and curl.
- Maintain a predictable docs-site publishing lifecycle with automated checks and named owners.
- Surface the top support issues with reproducible fixes and playbook steps so customer-facing teams can resolve 80% of tier-1 tickets without engineering intervention.

Audience:
- SDK authors, DevEx engineers, Solutions Engineers, Support engineers, Documentation owners, and Oncall SREs.

Scope and boundaries:
- Includes: Redwood SDKs (python, js), quickstarts, short templates (README/TOC/snippets), API examples for text generation, chat, embeddings, and streaming, and docs-site ops procedures.
- Excludes: internal RFCs, meeting notes, and ad-hoc runbooks in personal drives. Those belong in team Google Drive.

1) Templates and repository layout

Recommended documentation artifact types (and short templates are stored in the devex-docs-templates repo):
- Quickstart (1 page): goal, prerequisites, 5-min example, next steps.
- SDK Guide (multi-page): install, auth, basic usage, advanced patterns, migration notes, API surface mapping.
- API Example File: single-purpose snippet with copy-paste ready code, expected output, and test vector.
- Troubleshooting KB: symptom, reproduction steps, likely cause, canonical fix, mitigation, owner, links.

Filename and frontmatter conventions (enforced by lint pipeline):
- Filenames: kebab-case, hyphen-separated, short (e.g. sdk-python-quickstart-auth.json).
- Frontmatter fields: title, summary (1 sentence), last_updated, owner (team/person), labels, examples_supported (list).

Example quickstart template (plaintext snippet):
- Title: Quickstart: Python text generation
- Summary: Create a completion in two API calls using the Redwood Python SDK.
- Prereqs: API key, Python 3.9+, virtualenv
- Steps:
  1) pip install redwood-inference
  2) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
  3) python example.py (example file included)
- Next steps: see SDK Guide: advanced usage and streaming

2) SDK Guides: content requirements and examples

Minimum sections for every SDK guide (must appear in order):
- Install and quickstart (one code snippet to run)
- Authentication and config (env vars and client config example)
- First request (short snippet)
- Streaming examples (if supported)
- Error handling and retries (with recommended backoff)
- Performance tips (batching, cache usage, concurrency limits)
- Migration notes (for breaking changes)
- API surface mapping (table: SDK call -> Redwood API endpoint)
- Tests and CI snippets (how to run snippet tests against staging)

Code snippets: mandatory languages and style
- Provide examples for: Python, Node (JavaScript/TypeScript), and curl.
- Keep examples under 40 lines where possible and include expected response sample.
- Use real, minimal inputs (e.g., prompt: "Summarize the below text in one sentence") and a stable test vector for CI.

Example (Python snippet for text generation):

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.generate(model='open-redwood-1', prompt='Write a one-line summary of:

The Great Wave is a famous woodblock print...')
print(resp.text)

3) API examples and canonical request/response patterns

Canonical examples to maintain in examples/ directory (per-model, per-feature):
- text-generation: short completion, long completion, temperature=0.0 deterministic example
- chat-with-system: system + user + assistant multi-turn example
- embeddings: simple text -> 1536-d float vector example
- streaming: SSE or chunked response sample and client handling
- function/tool-calls: payload and expected structured JSON return

Each example file must include: language, minimal deps, exact command to run, expected output snippet, and a known-good test vector ID used by the eval harness.

4) Docs-site operating procedures (publishing lifecycle)

Ownership and roles:
- Owner: DevEx Documentation team (primary on call for doc correctness)
- Reviewer: SDK owner (must sign off for language-specific content)
- Approver: Product PM for feature docs when surface-area changes occur

Workflow steps (high level):
1) Draft in branch: include frontmatter and test snippet.
2) Run docs lint (md/json schema validation + snippet execution). Pipeline fails on missing fields or failing snippets.
3) Peer review by reviewer (two approvals required for breaking changes).
4) Merge and auto-deploy to staging site.
5) Smoke test: run the quickstart instructions against a staging API key (automated).
6) Promote to production after 24h of staging green runs or immediate for critical fixes.

Key automation checks in CI:
- Frontmatter schema validation (title, summary, owner, examples_supported).
- Snippet execution against a recorded test vector (strict mode: must match expected output for deterministic examples).
- Link-checker for internal cross-links and external references.
- Accessibility checks for images/alt text.

SLOs for the docs site (measured quarterly):
- Docs CI pass rate: > 98%
- Average time to merge documentation after PR: < 48 hours
- Stale docs over 12 months: < 4% of pages

5) Release cadence and maintenance windows

- Minor doc updates: merged daily into main and deployed on next scheduled site build (typically every 6 hours).
- Major version / migration docs: coordinate with SDK release schedule; freeze window 48 hours before SDK GA.
- Emergency fixes: use the hotfix branch and follow the staging smoke-test then immediate promotion path.

6) Top support issues and canonical fixes (current top 8)

Issue 1: SDK authentication failures (401)
- Symptom: client returns 401 on first request after onboarding.
- Likely cause: user set REDWOOD_API_KEY incorrectly or included stray whitespace. Commonly seen when copying from UI which adds a trailing newline.
- Canonical fix: Trim API key and ensure environment variable is exported in the same shell session. Example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<key>"
- Workaround: Pass api_key explicitly to the client constructor: RedwoodClient(api_key='xxxx')
- Owner: SDK team

Issue 2: Streaming client disconnects on long responses
- Symptom: streaming SSE connection drops after ~30s with partial content.
- Likely cause: default HTTP client timeout or a proxy terminating idle connections.
- Canonical fix: Increase client-side timeout and enable keep-alive. For Node: set fetch timeout and use eventsource polyfill with reconnection. For Python: use requests with stream=True and stream timeout config.
- Mitigation: recommend chunked heartbeats for customers using long-running streams.
- Owner: DevEx + Eng Serving Runtime

Issue 3: Mismatched embedding dimensions
- Symptom: embedding vectors are length N but customer expects M (e.g., 1536 vs 1024).
- Likely cause: using a different model than the one documented (model name aliasing) or outdated model mapping in SDK.
- Canonical fix: Confirm model id with `client.list_models()` or check the SDK mapping table; update SDK mapping and regenerate docs.
- Owner: Model Onboarding + SDK team

Issue 4: High token usage reported for short prompts
- Symptom: Unexpected high per-call token usage and cost.
- Likely cause: prompt formatting includes long system messages or accidental inclusion of hidden data (e.g., pasted logs). Also newline/JSON formatting can expand tokenization.
- Canonical fix: Provide canonical trimmed prompt examples and show how to compute token costs using our tokenizer tool. Add quickstart example using minimal prompt.
- Owner: DevEx + Product

Issue 5: Examples fail in CI due to nondeterministic model outputs
- Symptom: snippet tests fail intermittently in docs CI.
- Likely cause: deterministic test vectors were not labeled or examples rely on non-zero temperature.
- Canonical fix: mark deterministic examples (temperature=0) for strict matching; otherwise use fuzzy/regex matchers in test harness. Update CI config to allow fuzzy matching for non-deterministic examples.
- Owner: DevEx CI Team

Issue 6: Incorrect or missing TypeScript types in SDK examples
- Symptom: Type errors when copying TypeScript examples into customer projects.
- Likely cause: example uses unreleased type definitions or omits importing the client types.
- Canonical fix: add a minimal tsconfig.json to examples and include explicit import lines. Provide a short checklist for maintainers: update types on SDK release, run ts-check on examples.
- Owner: SDK TS lead

Issue 7: Local quickstart fails due to CORS when using browser examples
- Symptom: browser-based quickstart fetch fails with CORS preflight error.
- Likely cause: exposing an API key directly from the browser without a proxy; the public API blocks direct browser traffic for API keys.
- Canonical fix: update quickstart to use a small proxy example (serverless function) and emphasize security best-practice. Provide a runnable serverless example in examples/browser-proxy.md.
- Owner: DevEx + Security

Issue 8: Broken links after model rename/migration
- Symptom: docs reference model names that are no longer valid, leading to 404 or incorrect examples.
- Likely cause: model deprecation and alias changes not propagated to docs.
- Canonical fix: add model rename metadata to the model onboarding checklist; run a quarterly link-sweep for model pages and update aliases in the examples mapping file.
- Owner: Model Onboarding

7) Triage playbook for support engineers

Step-by-step triage (first 15 minutes):
1) Confirm reproducibility: ask for the minimal snippet and test vector.
2) Check client version and model name: request `pip show redwood-inference` / `npm ls @redwood/inference` and `client.list_models()`.
3) Re-run snippet in staging with provided test vector (support sandbox).
4) Review logs: request correlation_id if available and escalate to oncall DevEx if logs indicate 5xx runtime errors.
5) Apply canonical fix from KB and document ticket resolution steps.

Escalation rules:
- If reproduction shows a 5xx or 429 from Redwood service: open an incident and page Eng SRE.
- If snippet fails only in customer environment but succeeds in staging: involve Solutions Engineering for deeper environment debugging.

8) Metrics and feedback loop

- Weekly sync between DevEx and Support to review top 10 new tickets and verify KB accuracy.
- Monthly metrics reported to product: doc CI pass rate, mean time to publish, tickets resolved with KB article.

Appendix: Helpful CLI and snippets

Curl example (text generation):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"open-redwood-1","prompt":"Summarize: The Great Wave in one sentence","max_tokens":32}'

Node (short):
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference')
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'open-redwood-1', prompt: 'Summarize the Great Wave in one sentence' })
console.log(resp.text)

Checklist for new doc authors:
- [ ] Use quickstart template from devex-docs-templates
- [ ] Add frontmatter and examples_supported
- [ ] Add reviewer and owner info in frontmatter
- [ ] Run docs CI and fix snippet failures
- [ ] Add label(s) and update related_pages
- [ ] Request review (assign reviewer)

Contact and ownership:
- Primary owner: DevEx Documentation (devex-docs@redwood.ai)
- Oncall: see the devex oncall rotation page (internal link)
- Escalation: Eng SRE oncall and SDK leads (as noted above)

Change log:
- 2026-01-15: Initial published playbook (Maya Patel)
- 2026-02-20: Added top support issues and CI checklist; clarified streaming troubleshooting (Evan Chen review)

End of document.
